title: Child dies after being struck by vehicle at 196th and Tomlinson Road in Westfield
text:
A boy died early Wednesday morning after being struck by a vehicle Tuesday evening near a Westfield school.
WESTFIELD, Ind. — A boy died early Wednesday after being struck by a vehicle Tuesday evening near a Westfield school. WATCH FULL STORY BELOW The Westfield Police Department says the crash happened around 6 p.m. Tuesday at the intersection of 196th Street and Tomlinson Road.
That’s near the Westfield Washington Schools Administrative Office and Monon Trail Elementary School. Officers found the child with life-threatening injuries. An ambulance took the 7-year-old to Peyton Manning Children’s Hospital in Indianapolis in critical condition. The child, who has not been identified, died shortly after 5 a.m. Wednesday.
Police say the driver stayed on scene. It’s unclear what led to the crash, but investigators do not think the driver was impaired. WRTV spoke to Emily Ralph, whose children went to the same elementary school as the child who died. Ralph suggested better safety measures.
“It’s devastating. This is literally a parent’s worst nightmare. If it's speed bumps, if it’s a light, if it’s a crosswalk. Whatever needs to happen.
We have kids that need to be safe. ” Monon Trail Elementary School is down the street from the intersection, and some parents said children cross this intersection all the time to get to school. The Westfield city government said a formal request for a crosswalk was submitted in October, but the city declined the request.
A statement from the city government said it is unable to install a crosswalk without “appropriate pedestrian facilities,” and the other side of the road belongs to Hamilton County government, and that’s why Westfield cannot install a sidewalk and a crosswalk. Westfield Mayor Scott Willis said, “At that T-intersection where that young boy was hit, he was crossing the intersection. He was crossing through a private yard where there are no sidewalks.
On one side, there were sidewalks because it was the city’s side. On the other side, it’s the county’s side. ” The Republican mayor confirmed that the boy was 7 years old. The mayor said a crosswalk may not have prevented the crash.
“The young boy had crossed the road. His dad and a couple of kids were on the other side. He noticed that they had not crossed. So, he bolted back across the road into ongoing traffic.
I’m not sure if a crosswalk would solve anything there. We are taking it seriously. We are looking at all options right now. ” Ralph and other concerned parents said they will continue pushing for safety measures, whether it’s speed bumps, a crosswalk, or anything that could help prevent another crash.
